geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the broad courtyard with a smaller access notch to make the frontage response more explicit while preserving the dominant stepped mass.
Set the notch to the program-frame access side so the opening aligns with the verified street edge.
Increase legibility of the public opening at ground.
Keep the carve grounded and occupiable rather than abstract.

graph_edits.rationale: Retarget the public-threshold controller from a general courtyard to a smaller, more legible access carve so the verified frontage reads as an active ground seam rather than a sealed edge.
Align the carve to the program-frame access side so the opening actually addresses the verified road frontage.
Make the opening sufficiently wide to read as a public entry void and not a decorative dent.
Lower the carve height so the ground response is clearly occupiable and sectionally tied to the street threshold.

rationale: The candidate reads coherently in all four views as one dominant stepped block with a clear hierarchy and stable orientation on the parcel. The section is legible and the stepped upper mass has continuity, so the form is not merely a box. The main weakness is that the road-facing edge is too sealed: the blue frontage is acknowledged by proximity, but there is no strong public void, undercut, court, or entry seam that actively claims that edge. Parcel containment appears intact and the mass does not visibly collide across views. Programmatically it can support neighborhood-living/mixed-use as a compact capacity-aware street building, but it would be stronger with a more explicit ground threshold and void publicness at the access edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller and more tower-like than this low-rise neighborhood-living candidate; avoid over-verticalizing the form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped prism with a clear dominant mass and a legible section change; useful as a calibrated precedent for compact mixed-use massing.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office typology and tall block proportions differ from the candidate's compact street-building brief.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Strong void-driven massing: a central carved court/eye produces public legibility while preserving a clear outer envelope.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Tall tower typology is only loosely relevant; the candidate needs a ground-oriented civic threshold, not a tower gesture.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Upper mass setback and a differentiated crown can preserve hierarchy without collapsing the whole object into one box.

warnings: Public-threshold response to the verified road frontage is weak; the mass remains largely sealed at ground.

The stepped silhouette is coherent, but the access-facing ground needs a clearer carve or notch.
